#### 1. telangiectasia, impaired intellectual development, microcephaly, metaphyseal dysplasia, eye abnormalities, and short stature  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.462)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5223345)

**Proposed mechanism:** LRRC8A (HGNC:28518) —DISRUPTS→ Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065); LRRC8C (HGNC:28520) —DISRUPTS→ Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065); Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired intellectual development (HP:0010864); Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004308); Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired intellectual development (HP:0010864); Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065) —LEADS_TO→ Metaphyseal dysplasia (HP:0005974); Volume-regulated anion channel activity (GO:0030065) —LEADS_TO→ Eye abnormalities (HP:0000477). Loss-of-function mutations in LRRC8A and LRRC8C disrupt the function of the volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC). This disruption leads to cellular dysfunction and contributes to the overlapping and distinct phenotypes observed in both diseases, including impaired intellectual development, microcephaly, short stature, metaphyseal dysplasia, and eye abnormalities.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in LRRC8A or LRRC8C with a minor allele frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD populations would suggest these genes are not the primary causal factors for either disease, thus falsifying the hypothesis. Alternatively, if functional studies demonstrate that mutations in LRRC8A/C lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, rather than loss-of-function, this would also falsify the hypothesis. _(variant: rs757053375)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of VRAC in both diseases opens avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting cellular volume regulation. Modulating VRAC activity could potentially ameliorate downstream pathological processes contributing to the diverse phenotypes, offering a unified therapeutic approach for seemingly distinct rare conditions.

Loss-of-function mutations in TUSC3 (causing MONDO:0013290) and LRRC8A (causing MONDO:0012615) both disrupt the shared pathway of ion homeostasis and cellular volume regulation, ultimately leading to intellectual disability in both conditions.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies show that mutations in TUSC3 and LRRC8A affect completely independent cellular pathways with no discernible overlap in downstream effects on neuronal function, this hypothesis would be falsified. Furthermore, if specific variants in LRRC8A are found at high frequency in gnomAD and do not associate with MONDO:0013290, it would weaken the link. _(variant: rs74315372)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying the shared role of ion homeostasis and cellular volume regulation in both MONDO:0013290 and MONDO:0012615 could pave the way for therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways to ameliorate intellectual disability in both conditions. For example, modulating specific ion channels or transporters could offer a common therapeutic avenue.
